# Lifetime replay fixtures

`recording1.txt` through `recording4.txt` preserve the original accepted inputs for historical `lifetime-v1` replay. Their expected results are reproducibility baselines, not independent accuracy targets. `reference-sessions.json` keeps independent user-confirmed results separate.

The corresponding `.raw.txt` files contain original Normal observations, original timestamps, and changes to the recorded parsing context. Consecutive identical contexts are stored once. Fields unrelated to raw parsing or normal-row eligibility, such as UI events and tracing, are omitted. No parser results replace OCR text. Each file contains the SHA256 of its original observation journal. They are self-contained and do not require the original user's directories.

The `.occupancy.txt` files contain measured matches against previous accepted glyph masks, indexed by one-based recording sequence and current physical slot. Each record is `sequence|currentSlot,previousSlot,correlation;...`. A repeated current slot lists additional matching templates, not additional loot. The data carries no identity or quantity. Source feature JSON and observation journal hashes are included in each file. These measurements use the original image pixels and a correlation threshold of 0.90; no OCR was rerun for them.

The Core V3 regression uses the original validated name/quantity fallback and Core partial-text association, with no new interpretation supplied by its parser delegate. It replays the complete raw observations, including rejected fragments. The raw fixture also preserves parsing contexts for App parser integration tests. Its expected helmet totals are 576/264/2038/604; historical V2 on the same observations remains 576/264/2034/600. The independent references for the four recordings are 576/324/2050/604.

The new version recovers an independently image-verified fourth-recording wave from eight to nine groups of four helmets. This does not establish perfect recognition in every recording or exact arrival timestamps for repeated equal rows. The tests keep single-reading, unconfirmed extra-slot, name-glitch and fading-reappearance guards as separate requirements.

`recording5-unreadable.raw.txt` preserves all 3,115 normal frames of the September 13 recording with the independently confirmed 2,288 helmets. Original OCR fields, timestamps and parsing-context changes are retained; `visual-occupancy-v2` matches were recomputed from the original PNGs. Anonymous `visual-occupancy-only` rows are pixel measurements with no name or quantity. The file includes its original journal hash and measurement provenance. It contains no corrected OCR text or invented quantity evidence.

The App regression replays these measurements with the production parser and `lifetime-v4`, and expects 2,288. Suppressing only the unreadable fifth row's occupancy evidence at frame 428 or 2384 independently reduces that result to 2,284; suppressing both restores 2,280. This verifies the two specific recovered drops, beyond matching the final total. Removing all additional anonymous probes and rejected-row occupancy restores the recorded `lifetime-v3` input and its 2,280. All variants must have identical other item totals. Original image fixtures for the two lost drops and their preceding frames are in `normal-appearance/occupancy-unreadable-*.png` with separate source hashes. The additional synthetic Core guards exercise mixed items, unequal amounts, exclusions, incomplete interior rows, insufficient history and calibration gaps. Recovery is deliberately limited to a full five-row panel following a completely readable occupied prefix; ambiguous smaller stacks retain the historical behavior.

`recording6.raw.txt` preserves all 3,211 original normal frames and parsing-context changes from the September 13 19:45 UTC recording. The independently confirmed inventory is 2,428 helmets; the recorded counter produced 2,440. Its three image-verified false births first acquire readings at frames 122, 1426 and 2438. Their complete groups contain four, five and four physical arrivals respectively. The separate real arrival at frame 3022 must remain countable even though the full panel consists of identical item names and amounts. The ring in the inventory was a special-panel drop and is outside this normal-only fixture.

`recording5.fade.txt` and `recording6.fade.txt` add sparse measurements indexed by one-based sequence and physical slot. They preserve the contrast ratios and correlations produced from the original calibrated PNGs by `NormalLootFadeTracker`, including its reference history and resets. They contain no corrected OCR, quantities, birth labels or target totals. Journal and enriched-input SHA256 hashes are included. Recording 5 reuses the existing raw fixture byte-for-byte semantically; only the separate pixel measurements are new.

A matching final total is not sufficient evidence of correct event association. The image audit of recording 5 also found compensating errors in its previous 2,288 result: a false additional birth near frame 55 and another near 2896, plus a missed real arrival at 372. The fade-aware regression and audit distinguish these local groups from the independent inventory reference.
